note: Benchmarks that must share a fold (and leave each other out of in-fold features). Two reasons count. shared_items: identical item texts (items.content_hash) or near-duplicates (at least 5% of sampled items share distinctive 40-character text pieces). shared_source: the same evaluation run or exam series, so the same systems, harness and format. A name prefix alone is not evidence: helm_afr, helm_bbq and helm_thaiexam share no source, text or system set, and llm_bp_tag and llm_uncertainty_bench are unrelated. Systems shared alone are not evidence either: frontier models appear in many unrelated benchmarks (e.g. ikp and researchcodebench share 25 subjects, 0% text). Percentages are from scripts/lift/scan_benchmark_families.py (smaller benchmark checked against the larger); re-run it on a new data revision. Revision 54074453.

adaptivestep_family.evidence: 1,979 identical item texts, mostly GSM8K problems in adaptivestep and prox

swe_family.evidence: identical SWE task texts across all five

medhelm_family.evidence: same source_url (crfm.stanford.edu/helm/medhelm) and paper (arXiv 2505.23802); up to identical system sets; medhelm_medhallu/medhelm_pubmed_qa 27.0% and medhelm_med_qa/medhelm_medbullets 13.4% near-duplicate

openvlm_family.evidence: same source_url (huggingface vlmeval/openvlmrecords): one VLMEvalKit run; ai2d_test and mmmu_dev_val share 253 subjects (mmmu_dev_val has no labels, listed for completeness)

mmlu_family.evidence: mmlu and truthfulqa_mc: same source (open-llm-leaderboard-old), 150 identical systems; mmlu/mmlupro 7.4% near-duplicate

bbq_family.evidence: 60.7% of helm_bbq items near-duplicate bbq (BBQ in a HELM prompt)

igakuqa_family.evidence: same exam series (Japanese national medical licensing exam), same language and format; 0.8% near-duplicate
